A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAND research work. All 13 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original feature-selection experiments on nine benchmark datasets and MSI Grain, together with sensitivity and selection-consistency analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds Stochastic Gates comparison results and observations about its feature-selection behavior.

M1.justification: The SAND transformation, gain normalization, joint training, and final feature-selection procedure are retained. Remark 2.2 newly documents clipping gains to [0,1], consistent with the previously stated search-space bounds; this does not establish that the underlying algorithm changed.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same nine benchmark datasets and MSI Grain, including the same HAR70 nuisance-feature construction. The added comparator results and feature-count observations do not introduce different datasets or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds Stochastic Gates (STG) to the benchmark comparison in Figure 3/Table 4, HAR70 consistency comparison in Table 5, and MSI Grain comparison in Table 6. The four existing comparators remain, and Figure 4 retains its original comparator set. This is a focused, single-method extension.

E3.justification: The added STG evaluation introduces regularization-parameter searches and conditional retraining when gains fail to polarize. The retained experiments keep their stated splits, preprocessing, architecture, optimizer, feature counts, and training budgets. Removing 'from scratch' from the retraining description does not establish a changed initialization procedure.

E4.justification: Table 5 extends the existing HAR70 selection-consistency analysis to STG. Section 3 also adds a qualitative failure analysis: on Mice Protein, STG reportedly fails to select additional distinct features beyond k=37. The existing feature-count, noise-scale, and normalization sensitivity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over 10 benchmark trials, 10 HAR70 consistency runs, and five MSI Grain trials. STG uses these existing reporting practices; no new uncertainty-estimation procedure, seed disclosure, or increased run count is stated.

E6.justification: Existing scores remain unchanged, while Tables 4–6 add STG outcomes. STG becomes the highest-mean method on Fashion-MNIST (0.856 ± 0.002 versus the previous best 0.836) and ISOLET (0.936 ± 0.005 versus 0.927). It matches SAND's two HAR70 misselections and scores 0.911 ± 0.005 on MSI Grain, below SAND's retained 0.919 ± 0.002. These extend the comparative findings without changing SAND's measured performance.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, gain bounds, and linear-regression derivation in Equations (1)–(14) are unchanged. The clipping disclosure adds implementation information, not a new mathematical assumption or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract qualifies its performance claim: 'state-of-the-art' and 'outperforming or matching' become 'competitive' and 'often matching or exceeding.' This narrows the asserted consistency of competitive performance. The principal one-shot selection contributions and the conclusion's stronger performance wording remain.

C2.justification: v2 acknowledges that STG often avoids retraining and explains the exceptions through failed gain polarization. It also explains STG's absence from Figure 4 through the cost of regularization searches and discusses its difficulty controlling larger feature counts. These add specific qualifications to the comparison; existing SAND interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies training-time gain clipping and describes STG's search and conditional retraining. Code and dataset access instructions replace the anonymous repository address with the named CSEM SAND repository. The explicit 'from scratch' retraining detail is removed; existing hardware and other implementation disclosures remain.

R1.justification: The bibliography and related-work section are retained, but STG's positioning changes. Yamada et al. (2020) is removed from the footnote listing approaches SAND outperforms, becomes an explicit benchmark comparator, and receives acknowledgment of its ability to avoid retraining.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized abstract and experimental-prose revisions, expands comparator abbreviations, updates an author affiliation, and adds acknowledgements and a generic impact statement. The overall narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is redrawn with STG bars, adjusted axes, and an expanded caption. Tables 4–6 gain STG columns, with associated sizing changes. Table 2 moves from page 8 to page 9, and surrounding text reflows. The other figures retain their content.

improvement.justification: Adding a closely related stochastic-gating baseline makes the empirical comparison more informative, including results unfavorable to SAND, and the qualified abstract better reflects this mixed performance. The clipping disclosure also improves reproducibility information. These are useful but limited gains: STG remains absent from the varying-k plot, its search and dataset-specific retraining details are incomplete, and the conclusion retains broader performance wording.
